_readme: Per-module skill counts for the digital SAT Reading & Writing section, one entry per practice test.
Every practice test has three module records: module_1 (fixed difficulty), module_2_easier and
module_2_harder (the two versions a test-taker is routed into based on Module 1 performance).
Categories match this repo's existing db/categories/*.json buckets exactly (see README.md's category
table), with Command of Evidence split into qualitative/quantitative since that split is visible
question-by-question and the user asked for it split. Every module's nine counts sum to 27.
confidence values:
verified      - the user (or another trusted first-hand source) took this exact module and reported
the tally directly. Treat as ground truth.
reconstructed - Claude mapped a third-party question-by-question tag list (Walker Prep's Question
Type Inventory, or The Test Advantage's walkthroughs) onto this repo's categories.
The source used its own taxonomy (e.g. 'Logical Operations: Support', 'Reading
Comprehension') which had to be translated - see 'flags' on individual modules for
where that translation was ambiguous. Not independently verified against Bluebook.
partial       - only the vocab (Words in Context) count is confirmed; every other field is null.
missing       - no source with a per-question breakdown was found for this module as of 2026-08-19.
Known gaps: Module 2 is unpublished by any source found for Test 4 and Test 8 (both forms) and for
Test 7's easier form. Tests 9-11 have no question-by-question audit anywhere yet - they're recent
enough (Test 9/10 Feb 2025, Test 11 Feb 2026) that no third-party analyst has hand-tagged them.
Per the project's own Phase 2 TODO ('systematically add new database entries, must be 100% clean
data, needs strict approval') - treat every 'reconstructed' entry as a draft to confirm by actually
taking that module, the way Test 8 Module 1 already was.
A NOTE ON TWO SEPARATE FORMATS: College Board also publishes 'linear (non-adaptive)' SAT practice
test PDFs for students with paper accommodations - a genuinely different format (33 questions per
R&W module, 39 minutes, no Module 2 routing) that confusingly reuses the same test numbers as the
Bluebook app tests (e.g. there's a linear 'SAT Practice Test #8' PDF that is NOT the same content as
Bluebook's adaptive Practice Test 8). Every source used in this file explicitly audited the Bluebook
app version, and every full entry below is verified to sum to 27 questions - this file has no linear-
format contamination. Worth knowing if you're ever cross-referencing against another source, since
it's an easy mix-up.
RETIRED TESTS (2025-02-03): College Board removed Practice Tests 1, 2, and 3 from the Bluebook app on
this date - the first removal since the digital SAT launched. In their place: Test 7 (entirely new)
and Tests 8-10 (a mix of new questions and questions recycled from the removed 1-3). Test 4 was never
removed. Test 11 was added later, independently. Practically: a student today cannot select 'Practice
Test 1/2/3' in Bluebook anymore - they don't exist as standalone tests, though some of their content
lives on reshuffled into 8/9/10 in a way that does NOT preserve these modules' counts for those tests.
Every module belonging to Tests 1, 2, and 3 below carries "retired": true and a "retired_since" date
for this reason. They're kept in the file (real official Bluebook data, useful historical/comparison
reference) but should be EXCLUDED from any 'typical range for the current test' aggregate statistic -
the mock exam UI's MOCK_BUCKET_STATS in site/index.template.html only aggregates non-retired modules.
Test 8's Module 1 entry stays verified/trustworthy regardless of this recycling, since it reflects
whatever was actually served on a real live attempt, recycled content or not.
